On this page

HTTP API ​

In the default multi-agent layout each agent serves its routes at /<slug>/v1/*, and --mode single serves them at /v1/*.

Routes use the agent's HTTP auth chain, which defaults to localDevStrict(). --bearer-token and --allow-anonymous replace it with bearer or anonymous access. Built-in JSON routes return errors as { ok: false, error: "<code>", message? }, and MCP uses JSON-RPC.

Host routes ​

These routes need no auth.

RouteContract
GET /HTML index of mounted agents
GET /v1/agentsJSON index of mounted agents, multi-agent layout only
GET /<slug>/playground, GET /<slug>/playground/assets/:fileThe agent's playground page and assets
GET /docs, GET /docs/*Documentation site

--no-playground removes the index and playground routes, and --no-docs removes the docs.

Start a session ​

POST /v1/session opens a durable conversation.

bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/session \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"What can you do?"}'
# {"ok":true,"sessionId":"ses_…","continuationToken":"http:…",
#  "playgroundUrl":"…?sessionId=ses_…","traceUrl":"…/v1/session/ses_…/events"}
Body fieldContract
messageRequired user message
titleDisplay title
dryRunRun read tools and stub write tools
asOfISO-8601 instant with a timezone. Sets ctx.now() and rejects omitted, relative, or later declared tool time arguments
workspaceFilesRelative files added to the session workspace
purpose"eval" marks regression traffic

Send a follow-up ​

POST /v1/session/:sessionId continues an existing conversation.

bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/session/ses_… \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"continuationToken":"http:…","message":"Make it shorter."}'

The route accepts any chat session, including one a custom channel created. Each accepted follow-up returns a new continuation token. A message to a busy session interrupts the active turn. A stale token or a task session returns 409.

Stream or replay session events ​

GET /v1/session/:sessionId/stream is the live NDJSON feed.

bash
curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/session/ses_…/stream?startIndex=0'

It replays from startIndex, which defaults to 0, then follows new events. To reconnect without duplicates, pass the last index you received plus one.

GET /v1/session/:sessionId/events returns a one-shot NDJSON dump, or { sessionId, events, playgroundUrl } with ?format=json. Stream events lists the event types.

Manage sessions ​

RouteContract
POST /v1/session/:sessionId/stopInterrupt the active turn without sending another message
GET /v1/sessionsList sessions the caller owns
GET /v1/session/:sessionId/costPer-turn token usage and estimated cost

Under serve --dev on loopback, the list includes every principal's sessions.

Call a tool without a model turn ​

RouteContract
POST /v1/tools/:toolNameRun a server tool on { input, sessionId?, continuationToken? }

Tools covers session binding, busy sessions, and error codes.

Discovery routes ​

RouteContract
GET /v1/infoEverything discovery found, such as the model, tools, channels, and diagnostics
GET /v1/toolsServer and advertised MCP tools as { name, title?, source? }, optionally for one session or continuationToken
GET /v1/tools/:nameOne tool's schemas, effect rules, execution mode, and source. An unknown name returns 404 with the available names
GET /v1/logs?after=NRecent server logs and the next polling cursor

connectionErrors names any connection that couldn't list its tools.

List and download artifacts ​

GET /v1/artifacts returns the caller's { artifacts }, newest-updated first, filtered by kind, sessionId, and a positive limit. GET /v1/artifacts/:id/content downloads an artifact's file or blob. Artifacts covers tagging and record fields.

Call custom channel routes ​

Authored routes mount under /v1/channels/<id> with their declared methods and paths, behind each channel's auth chain. Route responses covers what a hosted caller gets back.

MCP endpoint ​

Both MCP routes use stateless streamable HTTP, so they take POST and return 405 for GET and DELETE.

/v1/mcp serves ask, check, and call_tool when server tools exist, behind the session API auth chain. /v1/mcp/tools serves only deterministic server tools, behind the CLI-level loopback, bearer, or anonymous auth chain. MCP connections connects one agent to another.

Playground eval routes ​

RouteContract
GET /v1/dev/evalsList discovered cases and eval config
GET /v1/dev/evals/runsList recent run snapshots, newest first
POST /v1/dev/evals/runsStart { filterIds?, tags?, timeoutMs?, verbose? }. Returns 202, 404 for no match, or 409 while a run is active
GET /v1/dev/evals/runs/:runIdProgress and the final snapshot
POST /v1/dev/evals/runs/:runId/cancelCancel an active run. Returns 409 when it already ended

Poll a run until it is completed, failed, or cancelled. A case must match one entry from each of filterIds and tags that you pass.

Dev-mode routes ​

These routes exist only under serve --dev, where schedules and reminders never fire on their own. POST /v1/dev/schedules/:scheduleId dispatches a schedule once and returns {scheduleId, sessionIds}. GET /v1/dev/reminders lists reminders, and POST /v1/dev/reminders/:reminderId fires one.

Status codes ​

CodeMeaning
202Accepted for asynchronous work
400Invalid body, query, or tool input
401No auth policy admitted the request
403The caller doesn't own the resource
404A named resource doesn't exist, or no eval case matches
405The route doesn't accept this method
409The resource's state rejects the request, such as a stale token or busy write
500A write-effect tool can't create its session workspace (workspace_unavailable)
